concepts.name: Adaptive Control
concepts.short_description: Controllers that adjust parameters online to handle uncertainty; model reference, self-tuning regulators.

concepts.name: Category Theory
concepts.short_description: Abstract algebra of mappings between structures; functors, natural transformations, universal properties.

concepts.name: Satisfiability
concepts.short_description: Determining if a logical formula has a satisfying assignment; SAT/SMT solvers; minimal unsatisfiable cores for conflict localization.

hypotheses.statement: Adaptation is constraint repair rather than gradient descent: every closed-loop observation becomes a clause over a discretised model/controller space, the adapting agent maintains a satisfiable clause set, and when the plant changes the set turns UNSAT; the MUS localises which past observations conflict with the new regime, so forgetting is targeted to the conflict instead of uniform in time. Experiment: switching plant, core-guided forgetting vs time-based forgetting.

Adaptation should be functorial: if controllers for subsystems compose into a controller for the whole, the adaptation operator should commute with composition (adapt(g o f) = adapt(g) o adapt(f)); SAT enforces the interface constraints. Experiment: adapt modules separately, recompose, and test whether the composite works without retuning vs non-functorial adaptation.

The SAT solver is itself the plant: its noise/restart parameters are control inputs, its unsat-clause trajectory is the output, and the random-SAT phase transition is a plant nonlinearity; an adaptive controller should be equivariant under instance isomorphisms (renaming), a categorical requirement. Experiment: MRAC on local-search noise near alpha ~ 4.2.

Persistent excitation is a Yoneda question: an unknown plant among a finite category of candidates is determined by its responses to probes, and the agent should choose probes forming a separating family, found by SAT as a hitting-set problem. Experiment: probes needed to identify the plant with SAT-chosen separating probes vs random excitation.

The adaptation target is a universal object rather than a point estimate: act only with controls valid in the limit (intersection) of all models still consistent with data; when that intersection is empty (UNSAT) the MUS names the models in conflict and drives targeted probing (dual control). Experiment: forbidden-state entries of limit-seeking vs certainty-equivalence control.

There is a phase transition of adaptability: as specifications per adjustable parameter rise, the closed-loop spec set passes from almost-always-repairable to almost-never-repairable, with adaptation time and MUS size peaking at the threshold. Experiment: sweep spec density, measure adaptation time and core size.

Regime changes are natural transformations: a regime maps a task category to behaviours; a regime shift is a family of components, one per task, tied by naturality squares; encoding squares as clauses lets an agent that re-adapted on a few tasks propagate the adaptation to unseen tasks. Experiment: accuracy of propagated components on unseen objects vs independent per-task adaptation.

Core-guided forgetting: the agent keeps a window of observation clauses over a finite model space; on UNSAT it extracts an MUS and deletes the oldest clause(s) inside the core only, instead of forgetting uniformly by age.

hypotheses.statement: Functorial adaptation: modules adapt locally but each update must satisfy SAT-encoded interface clauses so that the adapted composite equals the composite of adapted modules.

hypotheses.statement: Solver-as-plant MRAC: a local-search SAT solver's noise parameter is adjusted online by a reference-model law tracking a target decay of unsatisfied-clause count; the law uses only renaming-invariant statistics so it is equivariant under instance isomorphism.

concept_contributions.Adaptive Control: the MRAC update law and reference trajectory
concept_contributions.Category Theory: equivariance under the groupoid of variable renamings

knockouts.Category Theory: the law may use non-invariant features; the claim collapses to plain tuning (weak dependency)

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: a fixed noise value tuned offline, or a stagnation-triggered noise increase

questions.what_exists: solver state, noise parameter, reference trajectory
questions.what_can_transfer: the adaptive law across instance sizes and densities
questions.distinguishing_observable: median flips-to-solution vs best fixed noise and vs a sign-randomised controller

hypotheses.statement: Yoneda probing: the plant is represented by its response profile to a probe set; probes are chosen by solving a hitting-set SAT instance so every pair of remaining candidate models is separated by at least one probe.

concept_contributions.Category Theory: representable-functor view: an object is determined by its hom-profile

knockouts.Adaptive Control: no identification pressure; probe choice irrelevant
knockouts.Category Theory: probing is just active learning; the Yoneda framing adds naming only (weak)

questions.what_exists: candidate models, probe inputs, response table
questions.what_persists: the response profile of the true plant
questions.what_can_transfer: a separating probe set to a new family with the same response structure
questions.distinguishing_observable: probes needed to reach one consistent candidate vs random and greedy probing

hypotheses.statement: Limit-seeking control: at each step apply only controls safe in every model still consistent with data (the limit of the diagram of models); if no such control exists the MUS names which models disagree and the agent probes to split them.

concept_contributions.Adaptive Control: online control with the dual-control trade-off
concept_contributions.Category Theory: limit/intersection as the universal safe object

knockouts.Category Theory: it is minimax robust control over a version space (weak)
knockouts.Satisfiability: no conflict explanation; probes become random

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: minimax robust control over the version space with random exploration

questions.what_persists: safe actions common to all consistent models
questions.what_can_transfer: the rule 'act in the intersection, probe on conflict'
questions.distinguishing_observable: forbidden-state entries and steps-to-goal vs certainty equivalence

hypotheses.statement: Learned-clause gain memory: clauses learned from past closed-loop conflicts forbid parameter regions; on a new plant the memory is transported through a renaming functor if the plant is isomorphic to a past one, and discarded otherwise.

knockouts.Category Theory: memory reused naively and poisons non-isomorphic plants

questions.distinguishing_observable: speed-up on isomorphic vs non-isomorphic new plants

hypotheses.statement: Adaptability phase transition: with k specs per adjustable parameter, P(spec set repairable by adaptation) drops sharply at a critical density and adaptation time peaks there.

concept_contributions.Adaptive Control: adaptation as the repair process whose time is measured
concept_contributions.Category Theory: weak: the category of spec refinements only orders densities

knockouts.Adaptive Control: no repair process; plain random-SAT statistics

questions.what_can_transfer: the critical density to other plants
questions.distinguishing_observable: offset between adaptation-time peak and P(SAT) midpoint

hypotheses.statement: Bursting as core churn: in adaptation without persistent excitation, the sliding spec set alternates SAT/UNSAT; bursts in tracking error coincide with abrupt MUS turnover.

concept_contributions.Satisfiability: MUS identity over time as a diagnostic

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: bursts caused by excitation dropping below a threshold (classical explanation)

questions.what_exists: a slow adaptive loop with a window of specs
questions.what_can_transfer: the churn signal as an early warning

hypotheses.statement: Naturality-constrained transfer: after a regime shift, components learned on a few task objects are propagated to unseen objects by unit propagation over naturality-square clauses.

concept_contributions.Adaptive Control: online regime shift and sample-efficient re-adaptation

knockouts.Adaptive Control: one-shot fitting; no regime to track
knockouts.Category Theory: components independent; unseen tasks at chance

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: copying the adaptation from the nearest task, or composing maps along a spanning tree

questions.what_exists: task category, two behaviour functors, components

hypotheses.statement: Identification/design adjunction residue: treat identification (data -> model) and design (model -> controller) as a candidate adjoint pair; the round-trip residue (controller -> induced data -> re-identified model -> controller) measures certainty-equivalence error and predicts closed-loop failure better than parameter error.

concept_contributions.Category Theory: unit/counit round trip as a measurable residue
concept_contributions.Satisfiability: residue computed as SAT consistency of the round trip

knockouts.Category Theory: round-trip error is just prediction error (weak)
knockouts.Satisfiability: consistency check replaced by numerical distance

questions.what_persists: fixed points of the round trip
questions.distinguishing_observable: AUC of residue vs parameter error for predicting instability

hypotheses.statement: Compositional MUS credit assignment: in a diagram of controller modules, a fault is localised by an MUS over interface clauses and only modules in the core adapt.

knockouts.Category Theory: no modular structure; core is over flat clauses

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: adapt the module with largest local error

questions.distinguishing_observable: modules modified per fault and collateral loss on unaffected tasks

hypotheses.statement: Structure-preserving mutation: a population of controllers mutates only by composition-preserving rewrites of its module diagram; survivors must have SAT-certified safety specs; within a lifetime each adapts gains online.

knockouts.Adaptive Control: population search only (weak: adaptation is incidental)

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: random mutation with a fitness penalty for unsafe behaviour

questions.distinguishing_observable: fraction of certified offspring and fitness gain vs arbitrary mutation

hypotheses.statement: Backbone identity: the backbone of the specification SAT instance (literals fixed in all solutions) is the persistent part of the controller; adaptation should touch only non-backbone variables.
hypotheses.simpler_alternative: freeze parameters with low historical variance

questions.distinguishing_observable: backbone stability predicts which parameters change after a shift

hypotheses.statement: Adaptive quotient: the controller sees the plant only through a quotient of its state set; the quotient is adapted online to the coarsest partition for which the spec remains satisfiable.

concept_contributions.Adaptive Control: online refinement as the plant changes
concept_contributions.Satisfiability: feasibility of the spec on the quotient

questions.distinguishing_observable: partition size vs control performance frontier

hypotheses.statement: Conflict-seeking dual control: as CDCL seeks conflicts to learn, the controller chooses actions expected to produce model-eliminating conflicts, valuing an action by the number of candidate models it can refute.

questions.distinguishing_observable: models eliminated per probe vs random and greedy info-gain

lenses.name: Core-churn seismograph
lenses.rationale: If conflict localisation matters, MUS membership over time should carry information not in error magnitude.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: time series of sliding-window clause sets
lenses.transformation: extract one MUS per window; compute Jaccard turnover between successive cores
observables: lag from turnover spike to error spike
predictedSignals: core-guided deletion concentrates on pre-switch clauses
lenses.nullExpectation: turnover is uncorrelated with regime switches beyond what error magnitude predicts
failureModes: multiple MUSes make turnover depend on extraction order
window too short: every window trivially SAT
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: which observations conflict, not only how large the error is

lenses.name: Naturality-square defect ledger
lenses.rationale: Compositional and transfer claims reduce to whether squares commute after adaptation.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: finite category with two behaviour functors and learned components
lenses.transformation: enumerate generating squares and test commutation
predictedSignals: defects near zero under naturality-constrained adaptation
lenses.nullExpectation: defects equal to a shuffled-square twin
failureModes: bijective arrow maps make propagation trivial
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: structural correctness independent of task reward

lenses.name: Version-space thermometer
lenses.rationale: Adaptation and probing can be read as shrinking a counted solution space.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: set of candidate models consistent with data
lenses.transformation: exact model count by enumeration, log2
predictedSignals: SAT-chosen probes remove more bits per probe
lenses.nullExpectation: bits per probe match random probes
failureModes: count collapses in one probe for any policy on tiny spaces
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: an information currency comparable across mechanisms

lenses.name: Lyapunov certificate audit
lenses.rationale: Satisfying specs does not imply closed-loop stability; a stock control lens guards against that confusion.
lenses.transformation: solve discrete Lyapunov equation / compute spectral radius along the trajectory
predictedSignals: core-guided adaptation keeps spectral radius < 1 during recovery more often
lenses.nullExpectation: same certificate rate as time-based forgetting
failureModes: grids where all models are stable make the audit vacuous

lenses.name: Renaming-orbit equivariance probe
lenses.rationale: Categorical claims predict behaviour invariant under isomorphisms of instances.
lenses.transformation: run the same adaptive process on permuted copies; compare outcomes
predictedSignals: orbit variance at seed-noise level for equivariant laws
lenses.nullExpectation: orbit variance equal for equivariant and non-equivariant laws

lenses.name: Spec-density phase portrait
lenses.rationale: Tests whether adaptation difficulty has a threshold distinct from raw SAT statistics.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: random spec sets over discretised parameters
lenses.transformation: sweep specs-per-parameter; measure repair time and P(SAT)
predictedSignals: repair peak offset from P(SAT) midpoint
lenses.nullExpectation: peak coincides with P(SAT) midpoint (M7 is relabelled SAT)
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: distinguishes an adaptation-specific threshold from the generic one

lenses.name: Module blast-radius count
lenses.rationale: Compositional credit assignment should limit collateral change.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: diagram of modules with parameter vectors
predictedSignals: core-guided repair modifies fewer modules with less collateral loss
lenses.nullExpectation: same blast radius as largest-error-module heuristic
failureModes: single-module faults make all methods equal

experiments.hypothesis: Forgetting the clauses inside an MUS recovers from a plant switch faster than forgetting the same number of clauses chosen by age or at random.
experiments.mechanism: Scalar plant x' = a x + b u + noise (uniform +-0.05); candidate models (a,b) on a 16x16 grid (256 models). Each observation clause excludes models whose one-step prediction misses by > 0.1. Window of 40 clauses; on UNSAT (no model consistent) extract one MUS by deletion and drop its oldest member(s) until SAT. Controller: certainty-equivalence deadbeat toward a square-wave reference r(t) using the lowest-index consistent model.
experiments.intervention: Plant (a,b) resampled from the grid every 200 steps; 10 switches per run.
experiments.control: Drop-oldest: on UNSAT drop the oldest clauses (same count core-guided would drop) until SAT; also a fixed 10-step sliding window.
experiments.positive_control: Oracle reset: clear the window exactly at each switch.
experiments.observable: Recovery time per switch = steps until |x - r| < 0.1 for 10 consecutive steps.
experiments.success_criterion: Median recovery time of core-guided <= 0.7 x random-drop null twin AND <= 0.85 x drop-oldest, one-sided Mann-Whitney p < 0.01 over 300 switches (30 seeds x 10).
experiments.failure_criterion: Median ratio to drop-oldest >= 0.95 or p >= 0.05: core-guided is age-based forgetting in disguise.
experiments.alternative_explanation: Cores after a switch consist mostly of pre-switch clauses, so core-guided dropping equals drop-oldest; any advantage would come from noise-band tuning.
experiments.null_twin: Random-drop: at identical UNSAT times drop the same number of clauses chosen uniformly from the window (matched deletion count and timing; conflict localisation destroyed).
experiments.why_this_implementation: An enumerable 256-model space makes SAT and MUS exact by brute force, isolating the forgetting policy from solver heuristics; no learned function approximator is needed.
stupid_explanations: core-guided dropping is drop-oldest under another name
deadbeat control on a fine grid recovers in 2 steps regardless of policy
the noise band makes UNSAT fire spuriously, so the 'mechanism' is just a noise detector

experiments.hypothesis: Naturality-square constraints let an agent that re-adapted on a few task objects infer the regime-shift components on unseen objects.
experiments.mechanism: Random finite category: 12 objects, 20 generating arrows (random connected digraph), F: C -> FinSet with |F(c)| = 8 and random arrow maps. Hidden components eta_c are random permutations of F(c); G is defined by conjugation (G(f) = eta_d o F(f) o eta_c^-1) so eta is natural by construction. Samples (c, x, eta_c(x)) arrive online from 3 seen objects. One-hot encoding (64 vars per object) plus square clauses; a pure-Python DPLL with unit propagation predicts eta on the 9 unseen objects.
experiments.intervention: Regime shift from identity components to eta at t = 0; agent receives 30 samples.
experiments.control: Independent adaptation: unseen objects predicted by the pre-shift identity components.
experiments.positive_control: eta = identity for all objects (squares trivially determine components).
experiments.observable: Element accuracy of predicted eta on unseen objects.
experiments.success_criterion: Mean unseen accuracy >= 0.9 with squares AND (squares - null twin) >= 0.4, averaged over 20 random categories x 3 seeds.
experiments.alternative_explanation: Propagation is just composing known maps along paths (spanning-tree transport); categorical structure adds nothing beyond graph connectivity.
experiments.null_twin: Shuffled squares: same number and arity of square clauses, but each square links a random object pair through a random arrow map (clause statistics matched, true naturality destroyed; only instances that remain SAT are kept).
experiments.why_this_implementation: Finite categories with FinSet functors are exactly enumerable; DPLL over one-hot encodings is the minimal faithful solver. Displaces a GNN-on-graph default, which would blur squares into message passing.
experiments.size: 12 objects, 20 arrows, 8-element sets, 768 Boolean vars, 20 categories x 3 seeds
stupid_explanations: bijective arrow maps make any path transport trivial
accuracy driven by objects one step from seen objects
DPLL default assignment happens to match identity-like eta

experiments.hypothesis: An MRAC-style noise controller tracking a reference unsat-count decay beats the best fixed noise near the 3-SAT threshold, and its effect is invariant under renaming.
experiments.mechanism: Pure-Python WalkSAT on random 3-SAT, n = 60, alpha in {4.0, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3}; every 100 flips update p <- clip(p + gamma (u_obs - u_ref(t)), 0.01, 0.9), u_ref a geometric decay.
experiments.intervention: Adaptive noise law vs fixed noise.
experiments.control: Best fixed p chosen on 50 calibration instances per alpha.
experiments.positive_control: Oracle per-instance best fixed p (upper bound).
experiments.observable: Flips to solution (cap 2e4; capped runs count as cap) on instances solved by any method within the cap.
experiments.success_criterion: Median flips adaptive <= 0.8 x best fixed on 100 test instances per alpha in >= 3 of 4 alphas, paired Wilcoxon p < 0.01; orbit variance under 5 renamings <= 1.2 x seed variance.
experiments.failure_criterion: Median ratio >= 0.95 in >= 2 alphas, or sign-randomised twin within 10% of adaptive.
experiments.alternative_explanation: Any noise increase on stagnation helps; the reference model is irrelevant.
experiments.null_twin: Sign-randomised controller: same update magnitudes and times, random sign (matched noise variability; feedback destroyed).
experiments.why_this_implementation: Local search exposes one scalar control input and one scalar output, the smallest faithful adaptive-control plant; no learned policy needed.
experiments.size: n = 60, 4 alphas, 50 calibration + 100 test instances each, 5 renamings on 20 instances
stupid_explanations: adaptive-noise local search works for generic reasons unrelated to the reference model
the cap truncates distributions and hides differences
renaming invariance is automatic because WalkSAT picks clauses randomly

experiments.hypothesis: Acting in the intersection of consistent models and probing on conflict reduces catastrophic errors vs certainty equivalence at modest cost in steps.
experiments.mechanism: 64 candidate deterministic automata (6 states, 2 inputs, one forbidden state, one goal, shared start); true plant drawn uniformly. Agent keeps the consistent set; safe actions = those not reaching forbidden in any consistent model; if none are safe or none progress, take the action whose predicted next state splits the consistent set most (refutation value).
experiments.control: Certainty equivalence: plan with the lowest-index consistent model.
experiments.observable: Forbidden-state entries per episode; steps to goal; bits removed per probe (L3).
experiments.success_criterion: Forbidden entries reduced >= 50% vs CE with median steps <= 1.5 x CE over 1000 episodes; refutation probes remove >= 1.5 x bits per probe vs the null twin.
experiments.alternative_explanation: Robust minimax over a version space; nothing categorical or SAT-specific.
experiments.null_twin: Random probing: identical probe triggers and count, action chosen uniformly among allowed actions (matched probe rate; refutation choice destroyed).
experiments.why_this_implementation: Finite automata give exact version spaces; the limit reduces to a directly computable intersection.
experiments.size: 64 models, 6 states, 1000 episodes x 30 steps, 10 seeds
stupid_explanations: random automata rarely disagree near the start, so every policy is safe
the intersection is often empty, forcing probes that happen to be safe
